newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut Eurobond oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut Eurobond oversubscribed.

text.p: Bank of Beirut on Tuesday became the sixth Lebanese commercial bank to tap the international debt market with a three-year $50 million Eurobond issue.
The issue was slightly more than twice oversubscribed, Ziad Makkawi of Beirut-based Middle East Capital Group (MECG) which lead managed the issue with Paribas said.
"We had strong interest from the Gulf and good interest from Lebanese banks," Makkawi told Reuters.
It was the fourth issue on the Euro-market by a Lebanese bank this year and brought to $735 million the amount Lebanese commercial banks have raised on the international debt market since last June.
The Lebanese government, commercial banks and companies have raised a total of $1.185 billion in sovereign and commercial debt on the Euro-market since September 1994.
The BOB issue was priced at $99.884 with a coupon of 8.875 percent and a spread of 250 basis points over three-year U.S. Treasuries.
Jean Riachi, chairman of Financial Funds Advisors, a Beirut finance house, said the price was in the middle of the range expected by the market.

"It's a bit higher than some other issues, but if you take into account the size of the bank, it's good. It's almost a miracle for a bank of this size to issue bonds on the international market," he said.
"Three years ago this would not have been possible."
Bank of Beirut ranked 16th out of Lebanon's 82 banks in 1996 in terms of assets, which totalled $460 million compared with more than $3 billion for top ranked Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer.

Makkawi said that coming on the heels of BOB'ssuccessful share offering and listing on the Beirut Stock Exchange, the issue gave it the means to compete effectively for the next couple of years and put it in a very strong strategic position in the Lebanese banking community.
"It's very positive for BOB as a medium-size bank since it gives it a position comparable with the top tier banks in terms of debt offerings," he said.
The proceeds of the issue would be used to expand the bank's normal banking operations, Makkawi said.
